title: Pivot or Persevere
equation: Pivot Quality = (Data Honesty + Pre-Set Criteria + Decision Speed) ÷ 3
hook: If you decide whether to pivot after you see the numbers, your hope is making the call.
statement: Regularly decide whether to change your strategy or double down, using rules you set ahead of time.
explainer: Without rules written in advance, you'll explain away bad data. Pivoting isn't failing, it's using what you learned. Just change one thing at a time so the lessons don't get lost.
sop: Write your pivot and persevere criteria before the next cycle.
Compare the data to your criteria honestly.
If you pivot, change one thing: segment, feature, channel, or price.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Data Honesty 8, Pre-Set Criteria 6, Decision Speed 7. (8 + 6 + 7) ÷ 3 = 7.0. Higher means your pivot calls are fast and based on evidence. Lower means you're deciding on mood, after the fact, or too late.
question: Write down the one number that would tell you to pivot, before your next results come in.
closing_statement: Rules set in advance protect you from your own hope.
caption:
Principle Nº 291: Pivot or Persevere

If you decide whether to pivot after you see the numbers, your hope is making the call.

Regularly decide whether to change your strategy or double down, using rules you set ahead of time.
